value:
Three runtime traps in `bun build --compile` binaries that bit v1.0.0-beta.2 and were fixed in beta.3:

1. **NODE_ENV defaults to "development" at runtime** even though `--compile` implies `--production` at build time. Any `NODE_ENV === 'development'` check trips. Detect bun-compile via `process.argv[1]?.startsWith('/$bunfs/')` and short-circuit dev-mode logic before checking NODE_ENV.

2. **`__dirname` is baked at compile time**, not resolved at runtime. The build-host path (e.g. `/Users/runner/work/reverie/reverie/src/utils` on a GitHub Actions runner) becomes the runtime `__dirname`. Anything computing paths via `path.resolve(__dirname, ...)` will reference a directory that doesn't exist on the user's machine. `import.meta.dir` returns `/$bunfs/root` (the bunfs virtual filesystem root) — also not what you want.

3. **`process.argv[0]` is the literal string `"bun"`, `process.argv[1]` is `/$bunfs/<build-time-outfile-basename>`**. Neither is the path the user actually invoked. For the runtime invocation name, use `process.execPath` (it IS the invoked path or its symlink target). User-arg parsing via `argv.slice(2)` happens to work the same as Node (since bun matches Node's "runtime + script + args" shape), so Commander etc. parse fine.

POSITIVE: `os.homedir()` and `process.env.HOME` work correctly. Standard `fs.*` APIs work against the host filesystem (the `/$bunfs/` prefix only applies to bundled-source paths, not user data).

DETECTION HELPER: a single-line `process.argv[1]?.startsWith('/$bunfs/')` check is sufficient to identify "we're inside a bun-compiled binary" and override any logic that depends on Node-style argv or build-time `__dirname`.

VALIDATION-GAP LESSON: v0.0.0-debug.0/.1 only smoke-tested `--version` and the build matrix succeeding. Both of those happened to work on the broken binary because the banner+error were written to stdout AFTER the version line was buffered, and the build matrix only validates compilation not runtime behavior. Future debug-tag reruns for runtime changes need to exercise: data-dir writes (any `set` operation), MCP framing (initialize + tools/list + a tool call), and stdout pipe behavior (`rvr --version | head -1` should print exactly the version).
